title: Detention and Locker
premise: Ulyana Thornbury has spent three years perfecting invisibility: raising her younger siblings while her mother works night shifts, keeping grades high and questions low. When her AP English teacher assigns a college essay on the prompt 'What truth have you never told anyone?', Ulyana writes something devastatingly honest about the night she almost let her family fall apart — and accidentally submits it to a school-wide anthology contest instead of the private draft folder. As the essay circulates, her best friend Priya recognizes details Ulyana swore were fiction, forcing a reckoning about every secret between them. With the contest deadline, a truancy officer sniffing around her absences, and her siblings' fragile stability at stake, Ulyana must decide whether survival built on silence is worth more than a life built on truth — and in the end, she reads the essay aloud at the school showcase, losing Priya's approval but gaining an unexpected found family among the other kids who recognized their own hidden lives in her words.
about_author: Rosalind Whitlock is a former night-shift nurse who wrote her first novel during the quiet hours between patient rounds, drawing on years of watching teenagers hold up households no one knew existed. She lives in a small apartment full of plants with her two sisters, who still call her 'the boss' as a joke that stopped being a joke long ago.

chapters.title: The Art of Being Unremarkable
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A morning routine reveals her double life: packing lunches for Milo and Sasha, forging mom's signature, arriving at school invisible. Establishes her rules: head down, grades up, locker shut. Emotional beat: weary competence masking fear that one crack will collapse everything.

chapters.title: Prompt Number Four
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Mr. Okafor assigns the college essay: 'What truth have you never told anyone?' The class groans; Ulyana goes cold. At home she drafts a throwaway answer about 'the winter of seventh grade,' then keeps writing past midnight while Sasha sleeps against her shoulder.

chapters.title: Locker 214
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya narrates her decade of friendship with Ulyana and notices the cracks — the flinching at phone calls, the lunches skipped, the locker that never opens in front of people. She finds a hospital bracelet in the hallway trash and pockets it without knowing why.

chapters.title: The Wrong Folder
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Racing the bell, Ulyana uploads her essay to what she thinks is the private workshop portal — it's actually the district-wide Voices Anthology submission form. Confirmation email lands like a verdict. She spends the chapter trying to recall it and hitting dead ends.

chapters.title: Milo Knows Something
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, mostly Milo (age nine). Milo has been hiding his own secret — he's been skipping after-school care to visit mom at the hospital where she works a second job. His small rebellion collides with Ulyana's control, sparking the first sibling fracture.

chapters.title: Withdrawal Denied
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The anthology coordinator refuses to pull entries after the review window opens. Mr. Okafor, reading submissions blind, tells Ulyana one essay made him cry — she can't tell if it's hers. Rising dread; she starts rehearsing lies for when it publishes.

chapters.title: The Winter of Seventh Grade
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Ulyana's POV. The truth itself: the night mom was hospitalized, twelve-year-old Ulyana nearly called child services on herself to save her siblings, and instead lied to everyone — including Priya — about where they'd gone for six weeks.

chapters.title: Anthology Day
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The anthology posts online. Students read it in clusters; phones buzz through five periods. Ulyana watches her words travel the cafeteria like a lit fuse. Beat: public exposure begins, anonymous but ticking toward discovery.

chapters.title: Priya Reads It Twice
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya recognizes the hospital bracelet detail, the lie about the lake house, the specific way Ulyana described hunger. She confronts Ulyana gently; Ulyana denies everything with practiced smoothness. First real wound between them.

chapters.title: Truancy
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ms. Delgado from attendance flags Ulyana's pattern of absences — the ones she took caring for sick siblings. An official meeting is scheduled. The system she's dodged for years finally turns its head.

chapters.title: Sasha's Recital
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana skips the truancy prep meeting to attend Sasha's orchestra recital, choosing family over defense. Mom, exhausted between shifts, shows up late and sees Ulyana conducting the household like a general. Quiet, devastating scene of mutual recognition.

chapters.title: The Comment Section
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Other students begin responding to the essay — some cruel, some stunned into recognition. A boy named Deshawn posts that he lived 'the same winter.' Ulyana realizes she isn't uniquely alone, which is somehow worse and better at once.

chapters.title: Everything Priya Never Asked
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Ulyana and Priya. The friendship detonates: Priya lists every year Ulyana lied by omission; Ulyana says the unforgivable thing — that Priya's easy life made her safe to be around. Both walk away bleeding. Midpoint collapse.

chapters.title: Mom Comes Home Early
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Mom loses the second job and comes home at dawn to find the household running without her — and resents how well it runs. Mother and daughter fight about who was allowed to sacrifice. Ulyana's identity as 'the eldest' is named out loud for the first time.

chapters.title: Deshawn's Locker Is Next to Hers
chapters.summary: Deshawn's POV. Deshawn, who guessed the essay was hers weeks ago, offers solidarity instead of gossip. He shows her the abandoned art room where other 'anthology kids' gather. First glimpse of the found family forming in the margins of the school.

chapters.title: The Meeting
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The truancy meeting: Ms. Delgado, a counselor, and a social worker with a folder. Ulyana must choose between the polished lie that protects the family and the truth that could split them apart. She asks for one day to decide.

chapters.title: What Milo Told the Social Worker
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. Milo, terrified of being separated, tells the social worker the truth himself — that his sister saved them, that they're not broken, just tired. His honesty disarms the adults and shames Ulyana's instinct to hide. The siblings close ranks, changed.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The showcase committee invites the anonymous anthology author to read aloud — or stay silent forever. With the truancy decision pending and Priya gone, Ulyana drafts a new ending to the essay: not confession, but claim. She decides to sign her name.

chapters.title: Showcase Night
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Climax. In a packed auditorium, Ulyana walks onstage, names herself, and reads the essay — the winter, the lies, the price of survival. Silence, then Deshawn stands first. Priya, in the back row, doesn't stand, but doesn't leave either.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Fallout ripples: Mr. Okafor defends her to administration, Ms. Delgado closes the truancy case with support services instead of punishment, classmates who lived similar winters find each other. Not everything is fixed — but nothing is hidden anymore.

chapters.title: Locker Open
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya comes to locker 214 before first period. No apology speech — just the hospital bracelet, returned, and the question she should have asked years ago: 'Are you okay today?' Reconciliation begins honestly, without erasing the hurt.

chapters.title: The Essay I'm Sending to Colleges
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Final chapter: Ulyana submits her real college application essay — signed, true, unhidden. Mom takes a day shift so mornings belong to the family again. Last image: locker open, light inside, Ulyana walking down the hallway seen by everyone and unafraid.
